subject: Deletion quarantine criteria, backup purge timeline & escrow handoff
messages:
From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@medisyne.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@medisyne.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify backup purge / quarantine for legal holds

Hi Laura,

Quick question as we finalize our procurement review: can you confirm Redwood's default behaviour when a customer requests deletion for a set of user records but a downstream legal hold is later issued? Specifically: 

- Do deletions enter a "quarantine" window before backup purge? If so, how long is that window and is it configurable in the DPA?
- What is the backup snapshot purge cadence (daily/weekly), and are snapshots stored with the same retention as primary data?
- Can Redwood place encrypted snapshots in escrow (immutable) for a defined period if requested by the customer/procurement?
- Who are the subprocessors responsible for backup storage and are there any cross-border transfer implications?

We have an internal requirement to request an ability to trigger an emergency 7-day restore from backups in the event of an audit; is that possible under your current retention workflows?

Attaching our preservation template for reference. Appreciate the details so we can close the DPA addendum.

Thanks,
Jordan Mills
Head of Procurement — Medisyne Health
[Attachment: medisyne-preservation-request.pdf (pdf)]

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@medisyne.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify backup purge / quarantine for legal holds

Hi Jordan — thanks for the note and the template.

Short answers up front: yes, we can support a configurable quarantine (a hold period between deletion request and backup purge), we keep separate snapshot retention for backups (configurable tiers), and we can arrange an encrypted-escrow flow for snapshots under an addendum — subject to procurement terms.

Details below and I've looped in Legal (Karthik) and Privacy Ops (Kimberly) to propose exact language and operational limits.

Operational baseline (what we offer today):
- Default quarantine: 30 days between deactivation/deletion and permanent purge from backups. This is a safety buffer to allow short-term restores and accidental-erase recovery.
- Backup snapshot cadence: snapshots are taken nightly; snapshot-tier purge runs weekly. We retain weekly snapshots for 90 days by default and monthly snapshots for 365 days (configurable).
- Escrow option: we support encrypted snapshot escrow for customers who sign the escrow addendum — snapshots are held in an immutable storage class and can be retained for a negotiated period (30–365 days typical).
- Emergency restores: we can commit to a 7-day emergency restore SLA for escrowed snapshots (subject to notice and any legal approvals).
- Subprocessors: primary backup storage is handled by CloudStore Inc. (US), with cross-region replication to CloudStore EU for customers who opt into EU residency.

Next steps: Karthik, can you propose DPA addendum wording for the quarantine window + escrow? Kimberly, can you attach the retention matrix and note any operational exceptions (e.g., forensic holds, immutable snapshots)? Jordan, if you need 120 days as a minimum for certain PHI classes, flag which data classes and we'll run it through legal/procurement.

Thanks — Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@medisyne.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 13:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify backup purge / quarantine for legal holds

Jordan / team — adding legal context.

We recommend the following DPA addendum clauses (draft bullets):
1) "Quarantine window": Redwood will delay permanent purge of backup snapshots for a configurable quarantine period (Customer may request between 30 and 180 days).
2) "Escrowed snapshots": Upon Customer request and execution of an escrow agreement, Redwood will deposit encrypted, immutable snapshots into a designated escrow bucket under mutually agreed key management (KMS/HSM). Escrow retention period will be set in the addendum; restoration requests require documented authorization.
3) "Emergency restore and audit": Redwood will perform an emergency restore of escrowed snapshots within 7 business days of receiving a documented request from Customer's designated legal contact, subject to Redwood's verification process.
4) "Subprocessor disclosure": Redwood discloses CloudStore Inc. (backup storage), TransferEdge LLC (cross-region replication), and LogKeepers Co. (audit logs). Any cross-border replication to EU regions occurs only for customers who opt-in or where contractually required.

Operational exceptions to call out (we should surface to Medisyne): encrypted backups stored by third parties may have additional legal export/import restrictions; escrow increases storage and egress costs which should be captured in procurement pricing.

I'm attaching a short DPA addendum draft for procurement to review.

— Karthik
[Attachment: dpa-addendum-draft.docx (docx)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@medisyne.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify backup purge / quarantine for legal holds

Jordan — operational details from Privacy Ops / SRE: 

Retention matrix (high level):
- Tier A (hot primary): immediate deletion on request (logical delete), metadata tombstoned; snapshot references removed at next snapshot run.
- Tier B (cold backups): nightly full snapshots; weekly purge job; default retention 90 days for weekly snapshots; monthly snapshots kept 365 days.
- Tier C (escrow/immutable): created only with escrow addendum; stored in write-once storage for negotiated period.

Purge mechanics: 
- Logical deletion happens immediately (data becomes inaccessible). Purge job scans snapshots weekly and permanently deletes objects once quarantine period expires.
- If a legal hold is applied after a deletion request, we will pause purge jobs for the affected dataset; that dataset moves to a Quarantine state and requires documented legal notice to proceed to purge.

Restore process & SLA:
- For standard backups (non-escrow): standard restore attempts within 10 business days.
- For escrowed snapshots: 7 business day emergency restores as Karthik outlined.

Subprocessor notes: CloudStore Inc. (US) — default; TransferEdge LLC (EU replication) — only for EU opt-ins. We do periodic AICPA/SOC2 checks for both. If Medisyne requires only US residency, we can disable cross-region replication and limit subprocessors.

I've attached the retention matrix CSV for your procurement team to map cost impacts.

—Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Operations Manager
[Attachment: backup-retention-matrix.csv (csv)]

From: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@medisyne.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@medisyne.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify backup purge / quarantine for legal holds

Hi all — thanks for the clear breakdown. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) For PHI-derived identifiers (we'll label this Data Class A in the annex), procurement requires a minimum 120-day quarantine for backups even if the customer doesn't place a legal hold immediately. Is Redwood able to make 120 days the floor for Data Class A?

2) For escrowed snapshots, we need to confirm: who holds the encryption keys in the escrow model? Our preference is customer-managed keys (BYOK) where possible.

3) Please confirm any cost delta for 120-day floor vs. default 90-day. Jordan (procurement) — pending that, we'll queue DocuSign for the addendum.

Regards,
Jordan

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Mills <jordan.mills@medisyne.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify backup purge / quarantine for legal holds

Jordan — we can support a 120-day floor for Data Class A. Notes:
- Escrow BYOK: yes, customer-managed keys are supported for escrowed snapshots; we will need a KMS handshake and minimal operational runbook for key rotation and access approvals.
- Cost delta: Kimberly, please surface a delta and I'll include it in the procurement addendum.
- I'll route the DPA addendum + revised retention matrix to procurement and prep a DocuSign envelope once we have cost. If you want, let's schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to finalize terms.

Thanks — Laura
